title: ChanceChat
outcome: Random video chat where video only starts if both people say yes
summary: A prototype for one-to-one random video chat, designed around consent and safety. You start with text, and the server won't pass any video signal until both people have accepted. It is a working prototype, not a public service.

stats.label: People must agree before any camera turns on
Automated tests, plus a two-browser video test
Age-gated, with reporting and bans built in

sections.head: The usual design puts the camera first
sections.body: Random video chat apps usually switch the camera on the moment two strangers are matched, and moderation catches up afterwards. That is the part that goes wrong, and it is a product decision, not an accident.

sections.head: Consent before video, enforced by the server
sections.body: Build the safety into the protocol rather than the interface: an age check before matching, text first, video only when both people accept, and reporting, blocking and bans that work without a moderator watching every call.

sections.head: A prototype that refuses to cut corners
sections.body: People are matched one to one and chat in text. Either can ask for video; the camera is only requested once both have accepted, and the server drops every video signal until then, so a modified app can't skip the step. While video is on, each browser sends a still frame to a moderation hook every five seconds, and a flag ends the call. Reports keep the last 30 lines of chat, and three reports from different devices within a day trigger a 24-hour ban. The server refuses to start in production until a real age check and a real moderator are connected.
